column1: # Game profile of Batman: Arkham Knight (Switch, update 1.0.5 = v327680; the base NSP is a 7 MB stub). Plays on the Mac
# Format: see dm/games/README.md; bring-up and measurements in README.md beside this file
# Rocksteady's Unreal Engine 3 (package version 864) with Wwise, CRI Sofdec movies and Scaleform menus, SDK 14.3.0.
# The shaders are the global shader cache (GlobalShaderCache-Switch.bin) and the combined one in the Oodle-compressed package CombinedShaderCache-Switch.xxx (shader_split.py ue3_shaders).
# The engine's allocator runs on the host (patches.py, hle_uemalloc.c layout UE3); the game's task ring gets barriers (patches.py)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# The NPDM declares 32 MB of system resource (virtual address memory) and main never sets a heap. With the engine's allocator on a host malloc zone (outside the guest block)
# the game maps almost nothing in the alias region, and on iOS the block, that heap and Metal share the app's address space: a 2 GB block with a 1.375 GB alias region,
# as pull request #384 found on an iPad, where Engage's 5 GB block ran the heap out of address space (README.md, Memory). The node area is cut for this sdk build (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py)
